name: Meeting · Decisions and follow-through
description: For team and project meetings: what was decided, who owes what by when, and where the meeting stalls or drifts.

detectors.name: Decision made
detectors.what: the speaker states that a decision has been made or announces what the group will do
detectors.example: OK, so we're going with option B.

detectors.name: Action item
detectors.what: the speaker assigns a task to a specific person or asks someone to take an action
detectors.example: Priya, can you send the draft to legal?

detectors.name: Deadline set
detectors.what: the speaker states a date or time by which something must happen

detectors.name: Blocker raised
detectors.what: the speaker says something is preventing progress or depends on someone else
detectors.example: We can't move until security signs off.

detectors.name: Risk or concern
detectors.what: the speaker raises a risk, worry or possible problem
detectors.example: I'm worried we'll miss the launch window.

detectors.name: Ownership unclear
detectors.what: the speaker asks who is responsible for something or says nobody owns it
detectors.example: Who actually owns the billing migration?

detectors.name: Recap
detectors.what: the speaker summarises what has been discussed or agreed so far
detectors.example: So to recap, we agreed on three things.

detectors.name: Off-topic tangent
detectors.what: the speaker moves to a subject unrelated to the topic under discussion
detectors.example: Speaking of which, did you see the game last night?

detectors.name: Recognition
detectors.what: the speaker thanks or praises a person or team for their work
detectors.example: Great work on the demo, everyone.

detectors.name: Question
detectors.what: the speaker asks a question or asks for information
detectors.example: Where did you buy the code?

detectors.name: Commitment
detectors.what: the speaker promises or commits to doing something
detectors.example: I will send it over by tomorrow.

detectors.name: Agreement
detectors.what: the speaker agrees with or accepts what was said
detectors.example: Yes, that sounds right to me.

detectors.name: Disagreement
detectors.what: the speaker disagrees with, objects to, or pushes back on something that was said

detectors.name: Uncertainty
detectors.what: the speaker expresses uncertainty, hedges, or says they are not sure
detectors.example: I'm not sure, maybe it was Tuesday.
